**This endpoint exists to refuse, in the protocol's own vocabulary.**

SAML Single Logout is not implemented, and that is a decision rather
than a gap. Front-channel SLO iterates every service provider in a
session through the user's browser, and any one of them being slow,
unreachable or simply wrong leaves a partial logout — a user told they
are signed out of applications they are not. That failure is worse than
not offering the feature, because it is silent and the user acts on it.

So: `/saml/metadata` advertises no `SingleLogoutService`, and a request
sent here anyway answers a SAML `RequestDenied` status with a readable
reason instead of a 404, so an integrator sees the decision rather than
guessing at a missing route.

Ending the session at this service still ends it. A service provider's
own session is its own to end.
